results.label: this tree ships the M112 trading-window rule (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the parent tree IS the committed M111 release: it has no window module and its accounts table declares none of the four columns
the parent’s own schema has no window column, and the account it wrote carries the routine zone it selected
opening the parent’s file adds exactly the four window columns, and nothing else about the row changed
no window is invented for a desk that never had one: all four columns are NULL, so the state is `unset` and it blocks nothing
every inherited fact is preserved: the account row, the trades, the users and the guardrail state hash the same as the parent left them
the parent’s own routine settings survive the upgrade untouched, so the window did not reopen a schedule
the four columns an upgraded database inherits carry the SAME declared type, NOT NULL and default as the ones a fresh database is created with
and the SAME CHECK on each of them, re-created from the DDL rather than inherited: both sides or neither, the format, the unequal pair, the zone with the pair, the source list
the CHECKs are the ones that describe the rule, not placeholders
and the position difference is RECORDED rather than hidden: an inherited table appends the four columns last, the fresh DDL places them before the prop fields
the schema refuses half a window, two equal sides, a malformed clock and an hour the clock does not have
and it refuses a pair with no zone as firmly as it refuses a source the app never writes
while the real window IS accepted and stored exactly as written — the constraints refuse shapes, not the feature
the parent’s OWN code still reads the upgraded file: its account row and its trades are there, and the extra columns are simply invisible to it
reading it with the parent does not drop the window either: the delivered tree still sees the pair afterwards

scope: M112 migration: four additive columns, and no window invented for an existing desk: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
